parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the particular solution of the differential equation
$(x-1)(3x+2)\frac{dy}{dx}=5y$, $x>1$,
for which $y=8$ at $x=2$. Give your answer in the form $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\int\frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}\,dx=\int\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)dy$ M1
$\ln(x-1)-\ln(3x+2)=\ln y\ (+C)$ M1 A1
$y=\frac{K(x-1)}{3x+2}$ depends on first two Ms in (c) M1 dep
Using $(2,8)$: $8=\frac{K}{8}$ depends on first two Ms in (c) M1 dep
$y=\frac{64(x-1)}{3x+2}$ A1

questions.question_text:
(a) Express $\frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}$ in partial fractions.
(3)
(b) Hence find $\int \frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}\,dx$, where $x>1$.
(3)
(c) Find the particular solution of the differential equation
$(x-1)(3x+2)\frac{dy}{dx}=5y$, $x>1$,
for which $y=8$ at $x=2$. Give your answer in the form $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$.
(6)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$\frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{3x+2}$
$5=A(3x+2)+B(x-1)$
$x\to 1$: $5=5A \Rightarrow A=1$ M1 A1
$x\to -\frac{2}{3}$: $5=-\frac{5}{3}B \Rightarrow B=-3$ A1
$\int\frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}\,dx=\int\left(\frac{1}{x-1}-\frac{3}{3x+2}\right)dx$
$=\ln(x-1)-\ln(3x+2)\ (+C)$ ft constants M1 A1ft A1ft
$\int\frac{5}{(x-1)(3x+2)}\,dx=\int\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)dy$ M1
$\ln(x-1)-\ln(3x+2)=\ln y\ (+C)$ M1 A1
$y=\frac{K(x-1)}{3x+2}$ depends on first two Ms in (c) M1 dep
Using $(2,8)$: $8=\frac{K}{8}$ depends on first two Ms in (c) M1 dep
$y=\frac{64(x-1)}{3x+2}$ A1

$(2-3x)^{-2}$, $|x|<\frac{2}{3}$,
in ascending powers of $x$, up to and including the term in $x^3$. Give each coefficient as a simplified fraction.
(5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
$\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{a+bx}{(2-3x)^2}$, $|x|<\frac{2}{3}$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
In the binomial expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$, in ascending powers of $x$, the coefficient of $x$ is 0 and the coefficient of $x^2$ is $\frac{9}{16}$. Find
(b) the value of $a$ and the value of $b$,
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathrm{f}(x)=(a+bx)\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{27}{16}x^2+\frac{27}{8}x^3+\ldots\right)$
Coefficient of $x$: $\frac{3a}{4}+\frac{b}{4}=0\ (3a+b=0)$ M1
Coefficient of $x^2$: $\frac{27a}{16}+\frac{3b}{4}=\frac{9}{16}\ (9a+4b=3)$ A1 either correct M1 A1
Leading to $a=-1$, $b=3$ M1 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the coefficient of $x^3$, giving your answer as a simplified fraction.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Coefficient of $x^3$ is $\frac{27a}{8}+\frac{27b}{16}=\frac{27}{8}\times(-1)+\frac{27}{16}\times 3$ M1 A1ft
$=\frac{27}{16}$ cao A1

(a) Given that $y=\frac{1}{4+\sqrt{(x-1)}}$, complete the table below with values of $y$ corresponding to $x=3$ and $x=5$. Give your values to 4 decimal places.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5\\ \hline y & 0.2 & & 0.1745 & \\ \hline\end{array}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$x=3 \Rightarrow y=0.1847$ awrt B1
$x=5 \Rightarrow y=0.1667$ awrt or $\frac{1}{6}$ B1

parts.label: b

(4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Using the substitution $x=(u-4)^2+1$, or otherwise, and integrating, find the exact value of $I$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{dx}{du}=2(u-4)$ B1
$\int\frac{1}{4+\sqrt{(x-1)}}\,dx=\int\frac{1}{u}\times 2(u-4)\,du$ M1
$=\int\left(2-\frac{8}{u}\right)du$ A1
$=2u-8\ln u$ M1 A1
$x=2\Rightarrow u=5$, $x=5\Rightarrow u=6$ B1
$\left[2u-8\ln u\right]_5^6=(12-8\ln 6)-(10-8\ln 5)$ M1
$=2+8\ln\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)$ A1
